# nonArray

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** an array.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonArray() — Checks whether a value is **not** an array. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.4.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonArray<T>(value: T | unknown): value is Exclude<T | unknown, unknown[] | Array<unknown>>;
```

`nonArray(value)` is the same test as `!isArray(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

`Array.isArray` is the whole test, so an array from another frame counts and an array-like object — `arguments`, a `NodeList`, `{ length: 0 }` — does not.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type           | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not an array; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `Exclude<T | unknown, unknown[] | Array<unknown>>` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonArray("abc"); // => true
nonArray({ length: 0 }); // => true
nonArray(null); // => true
nonArray([]); // => false
nonArray([1, 2, 3]); // => false
```
